analysis.title: 'AI Jesus' Saves The World Again (But Tech Still Lagged); Bond Yields Tumble As Oil Spikes
key_insights: On Oct 15 the market moved against the data. Treasury yields fell despite hot PPI (energy) and strong retail sales and jobless claims. Tech was hit early, then recovered after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said CoreWeave will not need a bailout.

Index performance was mixed: Dow and Russell 2000 rose over 1%, SPX had modest gains for a second day, and NDX was the biggest loser. NDX recovered from -1.7% to about unchanged. The gains were mostly defensive and value rotation.

Goldman's Rich Privorotsky says the pain trade was long AI / short bonds and both sides are now unwinding. Credit concerns have entered the AI spending picture and the market is increasingly reading it as a growth shock.

AI credit stayed weak. CoreWeave bond spreads tightened but are still about 950bps, other data-center bond spreads widened, and hyperscaler credit worsened back to July wides while hyperscaler equity bounced slightly.

Goldman's Peter Callahan said risk appetite is 'not great'. He sees more debate than in July's momentum unwind about which worry is most acute into year-end: earnings, elections, rates/credit, ROIC or inflation. NDX forward P/E is back to about 21x, the lowest since the AI cycle started in 2023.

Momentum had its worst day in 3 months as momentum shorts were squeezed. Memory and semiconductors were hit again. Mag7 underperformed again, healthcare outperformed and energy equities were weaker despite higher WTI.

Goldman trading desk flow: activity was 6 out of 10, the floor skewed 15% to sell, exchange volume was +45% vs the 20-day average and SPX volume +37%. Long-only funds had a 40% sell skew on large notional, 70% sell skew in info tech, and only staples buying. Hedge funds were balanced with broad degrossing and aggressive consumer covering.

SPX bounced off its 50-day moving average and Nasdaq bounced to its trendline. Tomorrow's options expiration may remove some bearish positions. 7,690 is the key SPX level. A break below the positive-gamma cushion could turn the next move into a directional selloff.

Rates: yields fell led by the long end (30Y -11bps, 2Y -6bps), erasing the prior day's spike. 30Y is down 14bps from before CPI and yields are about 20bps below their spike highs. Rate-hike odds were unchanged to lower despite hot PPI and CPI.

Strategists attribute the bond rally to AI-bubble deflation fears outweighing inflation and growth data. A slowdown in AI debt supply eases pressure on the long end, and there is speculation that officials will curtail long-end supply. Bonds are ignoring energy for now.

Oil: WTI rose above $98, near one-month highs, on a Gulf of Mexico hurricane outage, strong exports and a large PADD 3 draw. Brent eased on an emergency reserve release. Attacks on container ships and tankers and Houthi-Saudi missile exchanges continue.

Jeff Currie says Brent at about $106 is a 'vibe contract' disconnected from physical markets. Dated Brent is near $130, Brent open interest hit its lowest since March 2025, and he calls the disconnect 'unpriceable risk' for hedgers.
Dollar fell overnight and ended about unchanged from pre-CPI. Gold rose back above $4,100 and Bitcoin bounced from support at $80,000.

Consumer staples now trade at higher forward multiples than tech, which last happened in the 2022 bear market. Bloomberg argues tech has stronger earnings growth, so the defensive tilt looks overdone and tech valuations already assume grim earnings.

market_movers.rationale: CEO Huang said CoreWeave will not need a bailout and its cost of capital is falling. Nvidia holds a stake of about $2 billion in CoreWeave. The comments lifted neocloud stocks and bonds and the broader market.
Stock and bonds rose on Huang's comments. Bond spreads tightened but remain about 950bps.

sector_views.rationale: Tech lagged, with memory and semis hit again and info tech seeing a 70% sell skew from long-only funds. Bloomberg notes tech's forward multiple is now below staples and argues valuations already price grim earnings.
Staples now trade at a higher forward multiple than tech while profit growth is low single digits and operating margins are falling.
Healthcare outperformed on the day in a defensive rotation.

earnings_insights: Goldman's Callahan suggests NDX forward P/E near 21x could let earnings 'do some work' into earnings season. This is a valuation comment, not a reported figure.
Financials drew a mixed reaction over the past two days of earnings. Bloomberg says the season has not yet given a convincing reason for a change in leadership.

tension_points.bull_case: Huang says CoreWeave's cost of capital is falling and it needs no bailout. NDX forward P/E of about 21x is the lowest since 2023, so earnings could support the market, and Bloomberg argues tech valuations already price grim earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Data-center credit is weak, hyperscaler credit is back at July wides, CoreWeave spreads are about 950bps, and long-only funds are selling tech. Goldman's Privorotsky reads the AI credit concerns as a growth shock.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below the SPX positive-gamma cushion near 7,690 would risk a directional selloff.

tension_points.bull_case: Growth and inflation data are hot, with PPI strong, retail sales solid and claims at multi-decade lows, which argues for higher yields and Fed hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: Strategists say growth concerns from AI outweigh inflation, so yields fall and the market is reluctant to price faster Fed hikes. Deflation fears from an AI bubble collapse and possible long-end supply curtailment also support bonds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Deutsche Bank's Zeng says bad AI news snowballing would keep growth concern ahead of inflation. A stabilization in AI credit would likely return focus to the inflation data.
